correctness.rationale: For a nonzero probe the residual is rank one: applying diag(1,ε) to the normalized perpendicular to (cos φ, ε sin φ) gives the norm ε/(cos²φ+ε² sin²φ)^(1/2). The Gaussian direction is uniform on the projective circle; continuity makes the swept angle a full interval. The distance d to the interval shifted by the orthogonality angle has mass α/π at zero and density 2/π on (0,(π−α)/2) for α<π. For α≥π the distance is identically zero. Inverting the decreasing residual as a function of d gives the stated tail, including the atom at 1 and the saturated part near ε. Averaging over d gives the stated mean. For b=(π−α)/2>0, subtracting (u²+ε²)^(−1/2) from the mean integrand gives a difference bounded by O(u) near zero and converging in integral to ∫₀ᵇ(csc u−1/u)du=log(2 tan(b/2)/b), even for b=π/2. Adding arsinh(b/ε) gives the claimed constant in the logarithm. A tangent substitution gives the one-point squared mean ε; Tonelli gives Tε. The probe zero has Gaussian measure zero, and the best rank-one error is the trailing singular value in both norms.
residual_risks: The bundled finite checks are recorded diagnostics, inspected but not rerun. The expansion is for fixed α<π, not an estimate uniform as α approaches π.
